text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - The UK stock market, weakened by pressure on drug and oil stocks, took a sharp dive after Wall Street dropped almost 50 points on profit-taking and worries about Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health. The FTSE 100 share index had pushed as high as 4,037.9 points in the first minutes of trade but retreated quickly. The FTSE index ended at 4,009.3 down 26.3 points.

FRANKFURT- Germany's blue chip DAX index ended bourse dealings just shy of its all-time high, buoyed by the firmer dollar, strong Bunds and surprising news from the telecommunications sector. The 30-share DAX closed floor trading up 11.82 points at 2,702.99, two points off a record of 2,704.74 hit on Monday. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,685.23.

PARIS - French shares finished in the red after rumours about Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health pulled Wall Street sharply lower, Russia later denied the rumours and said Yelstin was in satisfactory condition. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 14.83 points or 0.69 percent to 2,146.71.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended a volatile session slightly lower on average volumes as midday gains were erased by a weaker Wall Street beginning. "All in all we had a good session since we could largely keep yesterday's high levels", a dealer said. "If the Dow Jones closes stronger we are in for the next big jump". The All-share SPI index fell 0.31 percent or 7.56 points to 2,435.29.

TOKYO - Shares extended losses to close weaker, as most investors held back from buying, with the unclear political situation amid upcoming general elections casting a pall over the market. The key 225-share Nikkei average lost 167.70 points, or 0.80 percent, to finish at 20,870.83. The market will be closed on Thursday for a holiday.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng index closed at a record high, up 143.81 points at 12,250.57, as large buy orders from Europe pushed prices higher in the last hour of trade. The previous record close set by the blue chip index was 12,201.09 reached on January 4, 1994.

SYDNEY - The share market closed weaker after a slide in bank issues prompted investors to take profits across the board following the market's strong performance over the past few weeks. The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, finished 21 points lower at 2,310.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares nudged higher in modest trade as the industrials index pushed forward and offset a slight dip amongst gold shares. "The gold price only perked up quite late. If that had happned earlier it might have changed things," one dealer said. The All-share index closed at 7,059.1, up 12.2 points, Industrials gained 9.0 points to 8,267.4 and Golds eased 3.7 points to 1,742.8.
